result.text:
Done. `gradle test`: 29 tests, 0 failures, with `ImportTest.java` untouched.

## What was wrong

The new developer's code decided *what kind* of thing it had every time it needed to do something with it: `if (idType.equals("D")) ... else if (idType.equals("C"))` in `importCustomer`, `if (Character.isDigit(zipCode.charAt(0))) ... else if (isLetter...)` in `importAddress`, and `zipCode instanceof Integer` / `instanceof String` in `Address`. All the validation lived in the importer, duplicated (the "all digits + parse + range" triplet appeared three times, each error literal four or five times).

## The design now

**Types as classes, decided once at creation.**

- `Identification` (abstract) ← `DNI`, `CUIT` (`src/main/java/customerimporter/Identification.java:1`). Each knows its own type code, validates its own number **in its constructor** — an invalid `DNI` cannot exist — and answers `type()`, `isDNI()`, `isCUIT()`, `dniNumberIfNone()`, `cuitNumberIfNone()` polymorphically. `Identification.ofType(type, number)` resolves the creator through a map keyed by each class's own `TYPE` constant, raising `"Invalid identification type"` when there is none.
- `ZipCode` (abstract) ← `OldZipCode`, `NewZipCode` (`src/main/java/customerimporter/ZipCode.java:1`). The discriminator here is a condition, not a key, so `ZipCode.from(...)` asks each type `canBeCreatedFrom(...)` and creates the first that recognizes the string.
- `Customer` holds an `Identification`, `Address` holds a `ZipCode`; their `hasDNIAsIdentification`, `hasOldZipCode`, `...IfNone` methods are one-line delegations. `importCustomer`/`importAddress` are now just record reading plus `Identification.ofType(...)` / `ZipCode.from(...)`.

**Repeated code removed:** `Validation` (`assertThat`, `assertAreAllDigits`, `assertAreAllLetters`, `assertIsNumberBetween`); `NewZipCode` validates its embedded number with `OldZipCode.assertIsValidNumber`, passing its own error description, so the 1000..9999 range lives in one place; one method per error message; and `Customer.hasIdentificationOfType` replaces the condition both customer systems wrote by hand.

**Left alone deliberately:** the plain assertion `if`s (`assertValidCustomerRecord`, etc.) and the record-type dispatch in `importRecord` — those are the original starting code, not the identification/zip-code typing the exercise is about. `ZipCode`'s "unknown type" error still says `"Invalid identification type"`, a copy-paste bug of the original that `test29` pins down; it is kept with a comment since the tests must stay as they are.

The README has a "Solution" section with the same summary.
